fields.sample_size: doctrinal review of Spanish national and regional (autonomous community) water and social-measure legislation; no respondent sample
fields.effect_estimate: Spain has insufficient legal regulation of the human right to water for people at risk of poverty and exclusion; because normative competence is decentralised, social measures on water supply (e.g. Catalonia's Law 24/2015 protocol against cut-offs, a 100 litres per person per day minimum in some regions) are heterogeneous, so protection depends on the place of residence; only some autonomous communities (Andalusia, Asturias, Canary Islands, Catalonia, Madrid among those named) have such measures and five reflect user rights in their water laws. Argues for legal reform. Doctrinal; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: doctrinal legal analysis (comparative review of autonomous-community legislation)
fields.section: Full text: Analysis of national and regional legislation; Conclusiones
fields.exact_location: Analysis of national and regional legislation; Conclusiones

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a doctrinal analysis of the legal protection of the right to water in Spain, read in full text 2026-10-04. Regulation is insufficient and decentralisation yields heterogeneous protection by place of residence (e.g. Catalonia's Law 24/2015 anti-cut-off protocol). No empirical outcome data.
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds named regional instruments. Pure legal analysis; no outcome data (eligibility under criterion 3 is a doctrinal-evidence question, cf. A12).
